messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

**To:** Engineering leadership
**From:** Héctor Quezada
**Re:** Giving Q4 to technical debt

I'm asking to pull the platform team off the roadmap for one quarter. Four engineers, twelve weeks, debt work only.

This is an arithmetic case, not a preference. Our median PR waits 4.1 days to merge; last year it waited 1.6. CI runs 47 minutes and flakes on about one build in six, so most engineers push twice to get one green. Nineteen of the 31 production incidents we logged last quarter trace back to three services sharing a database schema with no owner. We already pay that bill, and it gets bigger every quarter we put this off.

Where the twelve weeks go, in order: split the shared schema so every service owns its own migrations; cut CI below 15 minutes by parallelizing the integration suite and deleting the ~200 tests that assert nothing; kill the v1 API, which carries 0.3% of traffic and blocks every routing change we want to make.

There is a cost. Four features slip. I would rather pick which four in October than watch them slip anyway in March. The alternative we've been running, a debt sprint every few months, has failed, because this work crosses service boundaries and doesn't fit in two weeks.

I'll report on those three numbers every two weeks. If none of them has moved by week six, end the quarter early and put the team back on the roadmap.

Swap in your own metrics before this goes out. The argument only works if the numbers are real.
